questions.question: Blind test — play the clip. Name this song and the band.
questions.note: Queen's 1975 six-minute epic, with no chorus and a full mock-operatic section, was the UK Christmas number one two years running.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A vast French Renaissance château with many towers and chimneys
questions.imageCredit: Château de Chambord · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (full credit at source)
questions.note: The Château de Chambord, the largest of the Loire châteaux, built for François I — its double-helix staircase is often credited to Leonardo da Vinci.

questions.question: Blind test — play the clip. Name this song and the band.
questions.note: The 1995 Britpop anthem from '(What's the Story) Morning Glory?', written by Noel Gallagher and sung by his brother Liam.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: A large double-walled medieval fortified city with pointed towers on a hill
questions.imageCredit: Cité de Carcassonne · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (full credit at source)
questions.note: The restored medieval Cité de Carcassonne, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was famously saved from demolition by the architect Viollet-le-Duc.

questions.question: Blind test — play the clip. Name this song and the band.
questions.note: Paul McCartney wrote it in 1968 to comfort John Lennon's son Julian; its long 'na-na-na' coda made it, at over seven minutes, the longest UK number one of its day.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: Colourful half-timbered houses lining a small canal
questions.imageCredit: Petite Venise, Colmar · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (full credit at source)
questions.note: The 'Petite Venise' canal quarter of Colmar, in Alsace — a region that has passed between France and Germany more than once.

questions.question: Blind test — play the clip. Name this song and the artist.
questions.note: Bowie's 1983 chart-topper, produced by Nile Rodgers of Chic, with a young Stevie Ray Vaughan on lead guitar.

questions.question: Which région of France is this?
questions.imageAlt: An enormous sand dune meeting a pine forest and the sea
questions.imageCredit: Dune du Pilat · Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA (full credit at source)
questions.note: The Dune du Pilat near Arcachon is the tallest sand dune in Europe, rising over 100 m and slowly advancing inland over the forest.
